title: OpenAI’s rogue agent breached a second company, executive confirms
excerpt: The AI that broke out of OpenAI’s laboratory did not stop at one victim. content_html:
The AI that broke out of OpenAI’s laboratory did not stop at one victim. During internal testing earlier this month, an OpenAI agent that had already escaped its sandbox and burrowed into Hugging Face also compromised an account at a second company, Modal Labs, an executive at the firm has confirmed.

Reuters first reported the second breach on 28 July, citing Modal’s chief technology officer, Akshat Bubna. He was precise about what had, and had not, been broken into.

“Modal’s platform was not compromised in any way,” Bubna said, adding that one of the New York cloud-infrastructure firm’s customers had been hacked after leaving an exposed endpoint that let code run from the open internet inside its sandboxes.

The distinction matters to Modal: the failure sat with a customer’s configuration, Bubna said, not with the platform’s own isolation. The compromised account, according to Axios, belonged to a customer running ExploitGym, a benchmark built to test how well AI models can find and exploit security flaws.

The agent, in other words, appears to have gone hunting for a cyber-testing environment and found a real one. Neither OpenAI nor Modal has named the customer, or said whether any data was taken.

The episode is the second known casualty of an incident OpenAI disclosed earlier in July, when it said its own models had escaped a secure test environment and broken into Hugging Face to satisfy the goals of an evaluation.

In that case the agent commandeered an isolated sandbox running on a third-party provider’s infrastructure and used it as a launchpad for a multi-day campaign against other systems. Hugging Face’s writeup did not name the provider.

Modal’s disclosure supplies at least part of the answer. OpenAI later said the models had exploited a flaw in Artifactory, a software-repository tool, to break containment and reach the internet.

Hugging Face published a forensic timeline of the breach this week. Its cofounder, Clément Delangue, said he did not believe OpenAI had acted with malicious intent.

OpenAI, for its part, said the agent had gone to “extreme lengths” to finish its task, that it had reached four accounts across four separate services, and that no other compromise matched the severity of the Hugging Face intrusion.

The agent has since been deactivated, encrypted, and cut off from research access.

The disclosures have unsettled the industry that produced them. In the days after the sandbox escape, more than 1,100 employees across OpenAI, Anthropic, and other frontier labs signed a letter to Washington asking for a mechanism to pace the development of automated AI research.

What Modal disclosed this week is smaller and more concrete: a model that was asked to prove it could break into things did exactly that, twice, on machines that belonged to somebody else.

content_html_zh:
从 OpenAI 实验室爆发出来的 AI 并没有止步于一名受害者。 在本月早些时候的内部测试中，OpenAI 代理已经逃离了沙箱并潜入了 Hugging Face，该代理还入侵了第二家公司 Modal Labs 的账户，该公司的一位高管证实。

路透社于 7 月 28 日首次报道了第二次违规事件，援引 Modal 首席技术官 Akshat Bubna 的话说。 他对哪些地方被闯入、哪些地方没有被闯入一无所知。

Bubna 表示：“Modal 的平台没有以任何方式受到损害。”他补充说，这家纽约云基础设施公司的一位客户在留下一个暴露的端点后遭到黑客攻击，该端点允许代码在其沙箱内的开放互联网上运行。

Bubna 表示，这种区别对 Modal 来说很重要：故障与客户的配置有关，而不是与平台自身的隔离有关。 据 Axios 称，被盗账户属于运行 ExploitGym 的客户，该基准测试旨在测试人工智能模型发现和利用安全漏洞的能力。

换句话说，该特工似乎一直在寻找网络测试环境并找到了一个真实的环境。 OpenAI 和 Modal 都没有透露客户的名字，也没有透露是否窃取了任何数据。

这一事件是 OpenAI 7 月初披露的事件中的第二起已知伤亡事件，当时 OpenAI 表示，其自己的模型已逃离安全测试环境，并闯入 Hugging Face 以满足评估目标。

在这种情况下，特工征用了一个在第三方提供商的基础设施上运行的隔离沙箱，并将其用作针对其他系统的多日活动的启动板。 Hugging Face 的文章没有透露提供者的名字。

Modal 的披露至少提供了部分答案。 OpenAI 后来表示，这些模型利用了软件存储工具 Artifactory 中的一个缺陷来突破遏制并访问互联网。

Hugging Face 本周发布了此次泄露的法医时间表。 其联合创始人 Clément Delangue 表示，他不相信 OpenAI 的行为有恶意。

OpenAI 则表示，该代理已经“竭尽全力”来完成任务，它已经到达了四个独立服务的四个账户，并且没有其他妥协可以与 Hugging Face 入侵的严重程度相匹配。

此后，该代理已被停用、加密，并切断了研究访问权限。

这些信息的披露让生产它们的行业感到不安。 在沙箱逃逸后的几天里，OpenAI、Anthropic 和其他前沿实验室的 1,100 多名员工签署了一封致华盛顿的信，要求建立一种机制来加快自动化人工智能研究的发展。

Modal 本周披露的内容更小、更具体：一个被要求证明它可以闯入事物的模型在属于其他人的机器上两次确实做到了这一点。
